confirmed.title: Heartbeat SFX is close to phase-inverted between L and R and loses about 10 dB on mono playback
confirmed.evidence:
**Cause.** stereo() builds the right channel as the left delayed by 12 ms. For the 52 Hz heartbeat thump, that delay is a 225 degree phase shift.

**In the source file.** heartbeat.wav has an L/R correlation of -0.77 (also -0.77 in the 0-100 Hz band, where nearly all its energy is). Its mono fold-down is -9.4 dB against stereo; uncorrelated noise beds lose 3.0 dB.

**In the mix.**
- SFX stem L/R correlation: -0.62 in SH16, -0.77 in SH17 and -0.75 in SH17B. Other shots range from +0.1 to +1.0.
- One beat at 60.8-61.4 s: L -20.5 dB, R -20.5 dB, but (L+R)/2 is -30.3 dB.
- ebur128 of the SFX stem over 59.9-66.8 s: -23.8 LUFS in stereo, -31.1 LUFS summed to mono. That is a 7.3 LU loss, against 1.8 LU for the SH14 SFX.
- The correlation of the whole final mix drops to +0.09, -0.06 and -0.04 in SH16, SH17 and SH17B. Elsewhere it is +0.5 to +0.97.

**Effect.** The heartbeat is the main tension cue under the shark sequence and his freeze. With mono summing (mono Bluetooth or smart speakers, the iOS/Android 'Mono Audio' accessibility setting), it nearly cancels. On headphones it sits phasey, inside the head.

heli_synth.wav and sub_hit.wav use the same helper (correlation -0.11 and +0.15). They do not cancel, but they comb-filter in mono (nulls at about 42, 125 and 208 Hz).

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. In synth_sfx.py, stereo() sets R = np.roll(L, 12 ms), and heartbeat() returns stereo(...) of a 52 Hz thump low-passed at 200 Hz. A 12 ms delay at 52 Hz is a 225 degree phase shift. Measurements: heartbeat.wav L/R correlation -0.77, mono (L+R)/2 9.4 dB below the stereo channel level; ocean_bed +0.97 / 0.1 dB, uncorrelated bubbles 3.0 dB. SFX stem: SH16 -0.62 / 7.2 dB, SH17 -0.77 / 9.4 dB, SH17B -0.75 / 9.1 dB; the beat at 60.8-61.4 s is -20.5 dB per channel but -30.3 dB in mono. Whole mix correlation is +0.09, -0.06 and -0.04 in SH16, SH17 and SH17B, against +0.48 to +0.88 elsewhere. In the decoded final AAC over 59.9-66.8 s, the band below 120 Hz has correlation -0.39 and loses 5.1 dB in mono, and the full band has correlation 0.00. heli_synth (-0.11, 3.5 dB) and sub_hit (+0.14, 2.4 dB) do not cancel. This is a real mix defect that only shows on mono playback, and most phone speakers barely reproduce 52 Hz anyway. Low.
